q: Equilibrium means a state of balance.
e: True. Equilibrium means a state of balance. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: There are three types of equilibrium: static equilibrium, dynamic equilibrium, and kinetic equilibrium.
e: False. Chemistry uses static equilibrium and dynamic equilibrium. Kinetic equilibrium is not a third type in this lesson.

q: Consider a book at rest on a table; the weight of a book gets balanced by the normal reaction force from the table to the book.
e: True. Consider a book at rest on a table; the weight of a book gets balanced by the normal reaction force from the table to the book. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In static equilibrium, both the forces are equal in magnitude and act in the same direction.
e: False. In static equilibrium the forces are equal and opposite, so nothing moves. Same direction would not cancel.

q: All chemical reactions are dynamic in nature.
e: True. All chemical reactions are dynamic in nature. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In a sealed bottle of soda, carbon dioxide is present only in the gaseous phase.
e: False. CO2 is in the gas space and also dissolved in the liquid. That two-phase split is a dynamic solubility equilibrium.

q: Inside the sealed soda bottle, the gaseous carbon dioxide is turning into a liquid at the same rate that the liquid carbon dioxide is turning back into a gas.
e: True. Inside the sealed soda bottle, the gaseous carbon dioxide is turning into a liquid at the same rate that the liquid carbon dioxide is turning back into a gas. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The maintenance of equilibrium in reactions between haemoglobin and oxygen in human blood is one of the processes involving human health.
e: True. The maintenance of equilibrium in reactions between haemoglobin and oxygen in human blood is one of the processes involving human health. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: The carbon cycle contributes to the equilibrium process that maximises the impacts of carbon dioxide on the environment.
e: False. Natural carbon-cycle equilibria tend to moderate CO2, not maximise its impact. The stem has the effect the wrong way round.

q: A dynamic equilibrium exists once a reversible reaction occurs under the appropriate conditions.
e: True. A dynamic equilibrium exists once a reversible reaction occurs under the appropriate conditions. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: Many chemical reactions go to completion, and the products cannot be converted back to reactants.
e: True. Many chemical reactions go to completion, and the products cannot be converted back to reactants. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Fuels are burned in the air to produce carbon dioxide and water, which is an example of a reversible reaction.
e: False. Ordinary combustion of a fuel in open air is treated as irreversible. Products do not turn back into petrol and oxygen under those conditions.

q: There is the forward reaction where reactants are converted into products, and the reverse reaction where the products are converted back into the starting reactants.
e: True. There is the forward reaction where reactants are converted into products, and the reverse reaction where the products are converted back into the starting reactants. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: In the forward reaction, reactants A and B combine to form product C, while in the reverse reaction, C decomposes into A and B.
e: True. In the forward reaction, reactants A and B combine to form product C, while in the reverse reaction, C decomposes into A and B. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: A reversible reaction is one that can occur in both the forward and reverse directions, and the conversion of reactants to products and the conversion of products to reactants occur simultaneously.
e: True. A reversible reaction is one that can occur in both the forward and reverse directions, and the conversion of reactants to products and the conversion of products to reactants occur simultaneously. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: Reversible reactions that happen in an open system eventually reach equilibrium.
e: False. Equilibrium needs a closed system so matter cannot escape. In an open system a gas product can leave and the reverse never balances.

q: When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions balance, the reversible reaction is in equilibrium.
e: True. When the rates of the forward and reverse reactions balance, the reversible reaction is in equilibrium. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: A closed system is a system that allows energy to enter and exit, but matter can neither be gained nor lost.
e: True. A closed system is a system that allows energy to enter and exit, but matter can neither be gained nor lost. A closed system can exchange energy with the surroundings, but matter cannot enter or leave.

q: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions stop completely.
e: False. Both reactions keep running. They just run at the same rate, so concentrations look constant.

q: In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue to occur at the same rate, leading to constant concentrations of the reactants and products.
e: True. In dynamic equilibrium, the forward and reverse reactions continue to occur at the same rate, leading to constant concentrations of the reactants and products. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Generally, the reaction begins with only the concentrations of products and there are no reactants formed.
e: False. You usually start with reactants and no products. Products then grow until equilibrium.

q: As the reaction proceeds towards equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants gradually decrease, whereas the concentrations of products gradually increase.
e: True. As the reaction proceeds towards equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants gradually decrease, whereas the concentrations of products gradually increase. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: After a system has reached equilibrium, the concentrations of all substances remain constant.
e: True. After a system has reached equilibrium, the concentrations of all substances remain constant. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: As the reaction proceeds, the rate of the forward reaction decreases and the rate of the reverse reaction increases until both reactions occur at the same rate.
e: True. As the reaction proceeds, the rate of the forward reaction decreases and the rate of the reverse reaction increases until both reactions occur at the same rate. At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal, so you still have both reactants and products.

q: At equilibrium, the rate of the forward reaction is high and the rate of the reverse reaction is low.
e: False. At equilibrium the two rates are equal. One is not high while the other is low.

q: In homogenous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in a single phase.
e: True. In homogenous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are all in a single phase. Equilibrium is when forward and reverse rates are equal, so concentrations stay constant.

q: In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are present in more than one phase.
e: True. In heterogeneous chemical equilibrium, the reactants and the products of chemical equilibrium are present in more than one phase. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: Any combination of solid, liquid, or gas states, as well as solutions, can exist in a heterogeneous chemical equilibrium.
e: True. Any combination of solid, liquid, or gas states, as well as solutions, can exist in a heterogeneous chemical equilibrium. Heterogeneous means more than one phase is present.

q: The reaction $N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO(g)$ is an example of a heterogeneous chemical equilibrium.
e: False. Every species is a gas, so that equilibrium is homogeneous. Heterogeneous would need more than one phase.

q: The reaction $H_2O(l) \rightleftharpoons H_2O(g)$ is an example of a homogeneous chemical equilibrium.
e: False. Liquid water in equilibrium with steam is two phases, so it is heterogeneous. Homogeneous would be a single phase.
